The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of one Sri.Gangadhara @ Gangadharappa @
Gangadharayya S/o late Pillappa, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 26.06.2023 at about 07.30 p.m, on Hosahalli - Arudi Road, near Shankar Narayana Rao's land, Hosahalli Grama, Sasalu (h), Doddaballapura Tq, Bengaluru Rural District, one Gangadhara @ Gangadharappa was a pedestrian at the road side and proceeding from Hosahalli towards Gowdanakunte, at that time, one Splendor Motor Cycle bearing No. KA-43-Y-2339 driven by one Mr.Prabhudeva along with one pillion Mr.Chandan and proceeding from Arudi side towards Hosahalli side, in a rash and negligent manner, with excessive speed and dashed against the pedestrian Gangadharappa and caused the accident.
Due to impact, said Gangadharappa fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.

Prior to accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 46 years and was working (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.1387/2024 as Coolie and Agriculture and was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. Due to untimely death of the deceased, the entire family has lost love and affection and suffering from mental agony, moral, social and economical support to a greater extent, as he was the only earning member of the family.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle and in this regard the Hosahalli Police have registered a case against rider of Motor Cycle.

The respondent No.1 being the LR's of the RC Owner and respondent No.2 being the Muthamma Alias Muthu Lakshmamma vs Srinivasa on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101203409/
2 insurer of Motor Cycle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with cost and interest to the petitioners.

sentences.text: 03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and has filed objections.

04. The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the rider of Motor Cycle and involvement of the Motor Cycle in the accident, age, avocation and income of deceased, dependency of the petitioners with the deceased, nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased and (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.1387/2024 expenses incurred by the petitioners and contended that there is inordinate delay in filing the claim petition, hence the petition is barred by limitation and admits issuance of policy in respect of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-43-Y-2339 in favour of respondent No.1 and their liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that the rider of Motor Cycle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence and there is no valid RC, fitness certificate at the time of accident and hence,
respondent No.1 has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy and the alleged accident took place due to sole negligence of the deceased himself and the compensation claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant and hence prays to dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with costs.

05. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, the following Issues has been framed by my learned predecessor:-
ISSUES
01 . Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Gangadhara @ Gangadharappa @ Gangadharaiah S/o late Pillappa?

02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Gangadhara @ Gangadharappa (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.1387/2024 @ Gangadharaiah S/o Pillappa was died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 26.06.2023 at about 7.30 p.m, on Hosahalli-Arudi Road, near Shakarnarayana Rao's land, Hosahalli,
Doddaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru Rural, due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-43-Y-2339 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & whom?
04. What order or award?
06. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 is examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15 and closed their side evidence.

(SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.1387/2024 12. Issue No.3:- This Issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Gangadhara, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner No.1 in her evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 46 years and was working as Coolie and Agriculture and was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great hardship and lost love and affection.
13. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records and SSLC marks card or even Aadhaar card of the deceased to show his exact date of birth.
However, in the absence of authenticated documents for the proof of age of the deceased, this tribunal has to consider Police and other documents.
In the petition, Police and hospital documents the age of the deceased is mentioned as 46 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has considered the age of the deceased as 46 years as on the date of accident.
As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors.

14.

sentences.text: In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 to 4 are the major daughters and son and petitioner No.5 is the mother of the deceased and they are dependents on the income of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi &
Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

sentences.text: Since deceased was (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.1387/2024 aged about 46 years at the time of accident and was self employee and he comes in the age group of 40 to 50 years, 25% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (16,000 + 4,000) = Rs.20,000/-.

Since there are five dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (20,000 - 5,000) = Rs.15,000/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.15,000/-.
As the deceased was aged about 46 years, the multiplier of 13 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.23,40,000/- (Rs.15,000/- x 12 x 13) towards loss of dependency.

16. In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others case, in respect to loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

17. The claimant No.1 is the wife, claimants No.2 to 4 are the children and claimant No.5 is mother of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners No.1 and 5 are entitled for Rs.48,400/- each towards loss of spousal and filial consortium.
In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130

19. Regarding liability:- In this case, the respondent No.1 has remained absent and placed exparte.

The respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal and filed objections and contest the matter (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.1387/2024 and to disprove the case of the petitioners and to prove its contention, its authorized signatory is examined as RW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the written statement averments therein.

During the course of cross-examination by the petitioners counsel she admits that she has deposed based on Police records and the accident occurred on 26.06.2023 and on that day accused also died due to accidental injuries and abate Charge sheet has been filed against him and they have issued policy to the new vehicle and witness says that they have received personal claim and OD damages according to the policy, they should see the evidence and say so.
Further witness says that they have produced Ex.R.3, as they did not present any other document other than the fact that they did not see the absence of a driving license in the final report.

RW.1 has produced Authorization letter, Insurance policy, Letter to respondent No.1 and Acknowledgment as per Ex.R.1 to 4, which shows that the offending Motor Cycle had valid insurance and the same is valid and is in force as on the date of accident and they have written letter to respondent No.1 regarding production of vehicular documents including driving licence of the rider of Motor Cycle.

(SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.1387/2024  20. Further, the Superintendent, RTO,
Yelahanka, is examined as RW.2 and he has deposed in his chief-examination evidence that the details of DL could not be traced out without furnishing the date of birth.
On searching the name by name of the DL holder through Sarathi application.
The particulars of DL could not be traced out and by entering the name of deceased and father name (Prabhudeva S/o Srinivasa).
But this witness is not cross-examined by the petitioners.
RW.2 has produced Endorsement as per Ex.R.5.
Ex.P.8

Charge Sheet shows the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against rider of the offending Motor Cycle for riding the vehicle without driving licence as on the date of accident.

Therefore, in view of the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of recent Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Akula Narayana V/s The Oriental Muthamma Alias Muthu Lakshmamma vs Srinivasa on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101203409/

"Where the contract of insurance is not disputed, even on breach of insurance conditions, this Court had allowed recovery (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.1387/2024 of compensation from the insurer by giving right to the insurer to recover the same from the vehicle owner.

Therefore, this tribunal is the opinion that, since policy of the offending Motor Cycle is valid and is in force as on the date of accident, since rider of the offending Motor Cycle rode the same without driving licence, it is a fundamental breach of terms and conditions of the policy.

Therefore,
respondent No.2 Insurance Company shall pay compensation amount to the petitioners with a liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending Motor Cycle.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.3 partly in affirmative.
21. Issue No.4:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,93,100/- (Rupees Twenty five lakhs ninety three thousand and one hundred only) with interest (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.1387/2024 at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment, with a liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending Motor Cycle.
The petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 to 4 are the major daughters and major son and petitioner No.5 is the mother of the deceased
were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 60-10-10-10-10, in the award amount together with interest.

On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled to get release 70% of the award through E-payment directly to her account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The petitioner No.1 is at liberty to draw periodical interest.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount of petitioners No.2 to 5 are meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in their favour through E-payment (SCCH-3) 19 M.V.C.No.1387/2024 directly to their account by obtaining their bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
